cases.description: Reported EBITDA vs Adjusted EBITDA bridge (reconciled by ESOP & lease add-backs)
cases.explanation: Both facts refer to Delhivery’s EBITDA for FY24, but they use different reporting bases. Fact A reports the company’s *reported EBITDA* of ₹127 Cr, which includes all items such as share‑based payments (ESOP) and lease rent. Fact B reports an *adjusted EBITDA* of ₹76 Cr, explicitly excluding ESOP and lease rent adjustments. Because the two metrics are calculated on different bases, they are not contradictory; rather, they represent two distinct measures of operating performance. The reconciliation is that the adjusted figure is derived from the reported figure by subtracting the ESOP and lease rent adjustments, yielding a lower EBITDA of ₹76 Cr.

cases.description: Economic Survey projection vs RBI Annual Report actual GDP vintage
cases.explanation: Both facts refer to India’s real GDP growth for FY24, but they are based on different reporting bases. Fact A is an advance projection of 6.5 % from the January 2023 Economic Survey, while Fact B is an actual provisional estimate of 8.2 % released by the CSO in May 2024. Because the scope differs—forecast versus actual—the values are not directly comparable and therefore do not contradict each other. The reconciliation is that the 6.5 % figure represents an expected growth rate, whereas the 8.2 % figure reflects the observed growth as of the provisional estimate. This is a classic forecast‑vs‑actual reconciliation.

cases.description: Genuine conflict with aligned basis and opposing assertions
cases.explanation: Both facts refer to the same entity (Beta Logistics), attribute (Audited Net Profit), period (FY24), scope (consolidated), and qualifiers (audit_status: final). The values reported are ₹150 Cr and ₹85 Cr, respectively, with no indication of differing accounting definitions, pro‑forma adjustments, or other reconciliatory bases. The evidence quotes explicitly state the audited consolidated net profit figures: "Audited consolidated net profit for FY24 was ₹150 Cr" versus "Audited consolidated net profit for FY24 was certified at ₹85 Cr." Since the metrics are identical in scope and reporting basis, the discrepancy is genuine and irreconcilable without additional context. Therefore the facts contradict each other.
